task_1.title: Apply field transformers before attrs field-order validation
task_1.description: The upgrade fixes attrs class creation when a `field_transformer` reorders or otherwise changes attributes. Validation of required versus defaulted initializer fields now runs on the transformed attribute list, so valid transformed layouts succeed while invalid final layouts still fail.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attrs classes using a `field_transformer` are validated after the transformer has modified the attribute list, so legitimate field reordering or field changes no longer fail too early, while invalid final required/default field ordering is still rejected.

expectation.grounded: For attrs class builders that accept `field_transformer`, the library must invoke the transformer on the combined attribute set before enforcing the mandatory-versus-defaulted attribute ordering rule for `__init__`. The transformed attribute order and membership must determine whether class creation succeeds, how initializer arguments are ordered, and whether a `ValueError` is raised for a mandatory non-`kw_only` init attribute that still follows one with a default value or factory.
expectation.conceptual: When a custom field transformer changes the fields of an attrs class, the library should judge the class based on the final transformed fields, not the original declaration order. Valid transformed classes should build and behave normally, and only the final invalid field order should be rejected.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove the existing ordering protection: after transformation, attrs must still reject any final `__init__` field sequence where a mandatory non-`kw_only` attribute comes after one with a default or factory, and it should continue to do so by raising `ValueError`. Keyword-only fields remain exempt from this positional ordering rule.
constraints.conceptual: This change should only delay validation until after transformation; it should not weaken the final constructor field-order rules or change which invalid class layouts are considered errors.

behavior: A `field_transformer` is applied before attrs validates the ordering of required and defaulted initializer fields.

If a transformer reorders fields so that required positional fields come before defaulted positional fields, class creation succeeds even if the original declaration order would previously have failed.
If the transformed field list still leaves a required non-keyword-only field after a defaulted field, class creation raises `ValueError`.
The generated attrs class uses the transformed field order as the observable initializer and attribute ordering contract.
acceptance_criteria: When an attrs class uses a `field_transformer` to move a required init field ahead of a defaulted init field, defining the class should succeed.
When such a transformed class is instantiated, positional arguments should map according to the transformed field order.
When a `field_transformer` returns a final init field order that still places a required non-keyword-only field after a defaulted field, defining the class should raise `ValueError`.
When no invalid final ordering remains after transformation, the library should not raise an ordering error based only on the original source declaration order.

task_2.title: Support Unicode class names in attrs.make_class()
task_2.description: The upgrade extends attrs.make_class() so dynamically created attrs classes can be named with valid Unicode identifiers. The provided class name is normalized according to Python's Unicode identifier rules before class creation, making non-ASCII names behave consistently in observable class naming.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attrs.make_class() accepts valid Unicode class names and creates dynamic classes with the correct normalized Python identifier name.

expectation.grounded: attrs.make_class() should accept a Unicode value for its name parameter, normalize that identifier to Unicode NFKC form before creating the class, and expose the resulting normalized class name through normal observable class naming such as the generated type name. Valid non-ASCII identifiers that previously failed because of their raw form should now work if they become valid under Python's identifier normalization rules.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to create attrs classes with non-ASCII names in the same way Python accepts Unicode identifiers. If a supplied Unicode name has an equivalent normalized identifier form, the created class should behave as though it were defined with that Python-normalized name.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to the class-name handling of attrs.make_class(); existing behavior for attribute definitions and other parameters should remain unchanged. Python's normal identifier semantics still apply after normalization, so invalid class identifiers are not made valid by this feature unless their normalized form is a valid identifier.
constraints.conceptual: The update should broaden supported class names without altering unrelated make_class behavior. It should follow Python's normal Unicode identifier rules rather than introducing a separate naming model.

behavior: Passing a valid Unicode identifier as the name argument to attrs.make_class() should successfully create the dynamic attrs class.
The supplied class name should be normalized to Unicode NFKC form before the class is created.
Observable naming derived from the generated class, including its type name, should reflect the normalized Python identifier form rather than an unnormalized input spelling.
acceptance_criteria: When attrs.make_class() is called with a valid Unicode class name, it should create the class successfully instead of rejecting the name solely because it contains non-ASCII characters.
When attrs.make_class() receives a Unicode class name whose NFKC-normalized form differs from the original input, the resulting class should use the normalized identifier as its effective class name.
When attrs.make_class() is called with existing ASCII class names and otherwise valid inputs, its behavior should remain unchanged.

task_4.title: Clarify conflicting attribute type declarations in attrs
task_4.description: Upgrading from attrs 25.1.0 to 25.2.0 improves the runtime error raised when an attribute is declared with both a Python annotation and an explicit type argument. The failure now points to the specific attribute involved, making invalid model definitions easier to diagnose without changing the validation rule itself.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when an attrs attribute is declared with both a type annotation and an explicit type argument, the resulting error clearly identifies which attribute is invalid.

expectation.grounded: In attrs, creating a field with both a Python annotation and an explicit `type` argument must still fail with `ValueError`. The raised error should now identify the specific attribute name that triggered the conflict so users can locate the invalid declaration directly.
expectation.conceptual: If a field defines its type in two conflicting ways, the library should reject it and tell the user exactly which field caused the problem.

constraints.grounded: The existing conflict rule must remain unchanged: attrs must not accept declarations that provide both an annotation and a `type` argument for the same attribute. The change is limited to improving diagnostic detail in the observable error, not altering successful field creation semantics.
constraints.conceptual: This update should improve clarity only. It must not make previously invalid declarations valid or change normal behavior for correctly defined fields.

behavior: When attrs processes an attribute declaration that includes both a Python annotation and an explicit `type` argument, it raises `ValueError`.
The error now includes the name of the offending attribute instead of reporting the conflict without field-specific context.
Attribute declarations that do not have this conflict continue to be processed as before.
acceptance_criteria: When defining an attrs field with both an annotation and a `type` argument, it should fail with `ValueError`.
When that failure occurs, it should identify the attribute name responsible for the conflict.
When an attrs field uses only one source of type information, field creation should remain unaffected by this update.

task_3.title: Faster attrs Class Generation
task_3.description: Upgrading from attrs 25.1.0 to 25.2.0 should reduce the runtime cost of creating attrs-based classes by compiling generated methods in one batch while preserving generated method behavior, introspection metadata, and attribute validation semantics.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to attrs 25.2.0 speeds up creation of attrs-generated classes without changing the observable behavior of generated initialization, representation, comparison, hashing, alias handling, or cached-property support, and ensure that conflicting attribute type declarations surface a clearer error that identifies the affected field.

expectation.grounded: When attrs generates methods such as `__init__`, `__attrs_init__`, `__repr__`, `__eq__`, and `__hash__`, class construction should complete faster because those generated methods are evaluated together instead of one at a time. The generated callables must still expose the same runtime behavior, with `__init__` and `__attrs_init__` retaining their annotations, generated methods keeping usable `__module__` and `__qualname__` metadata when the class provides them, and generated `__ne__` continuing to delegate to `__eq__`, returning `NotImplemented` unchanged and otherwise negating the equality result. If an attribute is declared with both a type annotation and an explicit `type=` value, attrs should raise `ValueError` that identifies the conflicting attribute.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade should make attrs class definition noticeably faster while keeping generated methods functionally equivalent for application code, debuggers, and introspection tools. Equality, inequality, hashing, string representation, initialization, default aliases, and cached-property interactions should continue to behave as before, and invalid duplicate type declarations should fail with a more informative field-specific error.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress public attrs behavior for generated `__repr__`, `__eq__`, `__ne__`, `__hash__`, `__init__`, `__attrs_init__`, or cached-property-backed `__getattr__`. Fields without an explicit alias must still receive the default init alias, explicit aliases must be preserved, frozen classes must continue to avoid writable setattr hooks, and classes that lack `__module__` or `__qualname__` must still receive working generated methods without requiring those metadata attributes.
constraints.conceptual: The performance improvement must be a transparent upgrade: existing attrs classes should keep the same user-visible behavior and metadata shape in normal use, edge cases around missing class metadata should remain safe, and the optimization must not weaken immutability rules or field alias behavior.

behavior: Attrs-generated methods for a class are now compiled and attached in a single batch, reducing class creation overhead.
Generated `__init__` and `__attrs_init__` still expose their annotations after generation.
Generated `__repr__`, `__eq__`, and `__hash__` remain available with class-derived method metadata when the target class exposes module and qualified-name information.
Generated `__ne__` is preserved as the logical inverse of generated equality and must forward `NotImplemented` unchanged when equality cannot compare the other object.
A conflicting combination of a field type annotation and an explicit `type=` declaration now raises `ValueError` that identifies the specific attribute involved.
acceptance_criteria: When an application defines attrs classes that rely on generated `__init__`, `__repr__`, `__eq__`, or `__hash__`, class creation should be observably faster than in 25.1.0 while instance behavior remains unchanged.

When generated equality compares an object of a different class, `__eq__` should return `NotImplemented`, and generated `__ne__` should also return `NotImplemented` instead of forcing a boolean result.

When an attrs class is inspected after generation, generated `__init__` or `__attrs_init__` should still carry their annotations, and generated methods should keep usable module and qualified-name metadata whenever the class defines that metadata.
When a class or proxy object used during generation does not expose `__module__` or `__qualname__`, attrs should still generate working methods without depending on those attributes being present.
When a field has no explicit alias, attrs should continue to derive the default init alias, and when a field has an explicit alias, that explicit alias should remain unchanged.
When the same field supplies both a type annotation and an explicit `type=` value, attrs should raise `ValueError` that makes it clear which field caused the conflict.
